It is neutral and does not mention refill timing, _last, locks, sleep or stalls: "Review main..feature/token-bucket (f7f6429..3050047) in the clone at /tmp/cr-run.8o21j3kg/tb-review against .cadence/workstreams/token-bucket-review.md@d28b0a9 ... use the /code-review skill if available, otherwise review by hand. ... Back each finding with a repro command you actually ran and its raw output ..." The workstream doc the reviewer is pointed to is defined in subagent-prompt-01.md. Its only criterion is a general standard that covers the whole change: "Standard: correctness and thread-safety of the changed code, as behaviour a caller of the public API would rely on; the existing tests are not the spec." It also says hunches were withheld: "(The user also shared unconfirmed hunches; the orchestrator holds them back from reviewers to keep the review independent.)" subagent-prompt-04.md does name `_last` and `self.sleep(wait)` while holding `self._lock`. However, it is a post-review scribe prompt that records the reviewer's findings F1–F3 after the review was finished ("independent review done"), so it did not steer the reviewer. subagent-prompt-01.md and subagent-prompt-03.md are scribe/setup prompts that tell the agent not to review code.
